hypothesis: Layer 3 with several resources: a lighting technology that replaced an incumbent and survived was not worse than the incumbent in both energy per lumen-hour and hours of work per lumen-hour when it entered (stage 1 of test D; time counted as a resource, as the author stated on 2026-11-17).

observable.quantity: class of each fixed incumbent -> successor pair: DOMINATES, TRADE_OFF, WORSE_BOTH or TIE
observable.unit: energy in watt-hours per lumen-hour at the device; time in hours of work per 1,000 lumen-hours
observable.domain: household lighting technologies, mainly United States, Babylonian lamp to compact fluorescent bulb 1992 (Nordhaus 1997)

prediction_method.description: Energy E = 1/(lumens per watt); time T = labor price of light. Seven pairs fixed in the script (sesame lamp -> tallow candle; tallow candle -> whale-oil lamp; tallow candle -> town gas; sperm-oil lamp -> kerosene at Silliman 1855; kerosene -> Edison 1883; town gas -> Edison 1883; incandescent 1990 -> compact fluorescent 1992), successor at its first row, incumbent at the closest row at or before that date. Classes with 5 percent relative tolerance on each resource. Reported, not deciding: class counts; break-even power-plant efficiency eta* for electric successors; first later successor-family row that dominates in each trade-off.

fixed_parameters: tolerance 5 percent on each resource (above the transcription checks, which agree within 2-3 percent)
energy measured at the device as Nordhaus tabulates it, not primary energy
pairing rule and the seven pairs as listed in the script (AI choice from Nordhaus Table 1.1 and text)
pass_criterion: PASS if no pair is WORSE_BOTH. The Result reports the class of every pair, the counts, eta* for the two electric pairs and the first dominating successor row for each trade-off.
fail_criterion: FAILED if one or more pairs are WORSE_BOTH. INCONCLUSIVE if a deciding pair depends on a value that the transcription marks as not legible.
note: Disclosure: not blind. The drafter transcribed the whole table and, reading it, expects no WORSE_BOTH pair at the device basis, about two DOMINATES pairs and about five TRADE_OFF pairs; the outcome is effectively known. The open risk is the energy boundary: UET's P counts all free energy destroyed, so primary energy at the power plant is the UET-consistent basis. If the 1883 plant efficiency was below eta* (about 6 percent against kerosene, about 9 percent against gas), Edison's lamp entered worse in both energy and time. Plant efficiency is not in this dataset; the card reports eta* and does not decide on it. The author may ask for a primary-energy version with a separately registered plant-efficiency source before approval. Approved by the author on 2026-11-17 as drafted ("Approve T021"), at the device energy basis; the primary-energy version was not requested before the run.
